UFC Elo ratings

Every card, one fight at a time
Pound-for-pound combines every division into one shared ladder. Cross-division comparisons only connect through champ-champs, catchweights, and fighters who moved up or down in weight — this is inherently less rigorous than the division-specific numbers, which stay on firm footing since fighters within a division actually compete against each other regularly.

Top 15 per division among fighters active in the trailing 24 months — two years of inactivity drops a fighter from this view. Retired or released fighters aren't manually removed; they simply age out on their own once two years pass since their last fight, so a name may briefly linger here after leaving the roster. This tracks per division: a fighter who's moved up or down in weight keeps their old division's ranking frozen until two years pass there specifically, even while actively fighting elsewhere — so a fighter can stay #1 in a division they no longer compete in. Reigning champion pinned above the list where known. Toggle to Overall (P4P) above for a single combined top 15 across every division instead.
The next three scheduled UFC events, always. Each fighter's rank reflects their position in the trailing 24 months, as of today — this is a pre-fight snapshot, not a prediction. "[Division] debut" means the fighter has a UFC record but not at this specific weight class before — they're moving up or down for this fight, distinct from a true "UFC debut" with no record at all. Compiled from Wikipedia's List of UFC events plus manually-provided updates, refreshed at least weekly; cards can still change before fight week, especially further out.
